head: 14bac80
target: A repo opts into the quiz gate with a tracked marker file instead of a git setting in each clone; the session hook installs the pre-push hook in every clone that has the marker.
incidental: usage text of the quizgate commands
selftest moved to the top-level scripts directory
SKILL.md wording for the new install
agent-mode.md wording on spawning the examiners

questions.prompt: The old install set a git setting in each clone, pointing at a hooks directory the repo carried. Why did that design lose?

options.label: The setting lived in one clone only, so a fresh clone pushed ungated.
Git refuses to run a hook from a directory the repo tracks.
The old hook could not tell which commits had a passed quiz.

key_points: The git setting lived in one clone's config, so it never reached a fresh clone.
A fresh clone pushed ungated until its author opted in there again.

questions.prompt: A repo opts in once, and its author commits the marker file. What does every later clone of that repo get?

options.label: The marker file, and a session hook that then installs the pre-push hook in that clone.
The marker file, and a git setting that each clone copies from the remote.
The pre-push hook itself, tracked in the repo like any other file.

key_points: The tracked marker file carries the opt-in to every clone.
The session hook installs the pre-push hook in every clone that has the marker.
The hook is never tracked; it lives in the clone's private hooks directory.

questions.prompt: Why does the hook run the gate from the author's personal bin directory, not straight from the plugin's install directory?

options.label: The personal bin directory stays put across plugin updates, and a plain shell finds it.
Git only runs scripts that live under the author's home directory.
The plugin's install directory is not readable while a push is running.

key_points: The plugin's install path changes on every update, so a hook fixed to it would break.
The copy in the personal bin directory lets the gate run with no plugin session loaded.

questions.prompt: A push runs where the hook cannot find the gate script anywhere it looks. What happens to the push?

options.label: Blocked, with a message that says how to install the gate.
Allowed, because a push that cannot be checked must not be held up.
Allowed once, and the missing gate is noted for the next push.

key_points: The push is blocked, not allowed.
The gate fails closed: a push it cannot check never goes through.
The message tells the author how to install the gate.

questions.prompt: A clone already has the author's own pre-push hook, one this change did not write. Which are true?

options.label: Install refuses and prints the line the author must add.
The author's hook file is left unchanged.
Install adds the gate line to the author's hook for them.
Install moves the old hook aside and writes its own.

key_points: Install never overwrites a hook it did not write.
It prints the one line the author must add by hand.
Over its own hook, install changes nothing.

questions.prompt: A new teammate clones the opted-in repo on a fresh machine and pushes the same day. No session hook has run there yet. Is the push gated? What turns the gate on?
key_points: No. The clone has the marker but no pre-push hook yet.
The session hook runs the sync command, which sees the marker and writes the hook; a hand-run opt-in does the same.
From then on, a push is blocked until a quiz covers its commits.
The same run puts a copy of the gate on the path for plain shells.
